title: Pausing, Restarting and Ending an Office Pantry & Beverage Program Agreement
content:
A client may stop standing deliveries without ending the programme, for a building closure, a floor move or a seasonal shutdown. These terms govern a pause, a restart and the end of an Office Pantry & Beverage Program agreement.

**Article 1 — when the work is taken.** A pause, a restart or a closure is only worked while the programme stands active, paused or closed, and a proposal is withdrawn rather than paused. The status standing on the programme, together with any first day of pause recorded against it, is read from Larkspur Table's own record of that programme before the work is taken.

**Article 2 — the length of a pause.** A pause shorter than the minimum printed against the tier is handled as a skipped delivery, and paused days accumulate against the contract year ceiling printed against the same tier.

**Article 3 — the programme while paused.** While paused the standby charge printed against the tier replaces the programme fee, and perishable stock is removed at the start of the pause without charge.

**Article 4 — restarting.** Restarting needs the notice printed against the tier, counted in calendar days, so that the standing list can be rebuilt before the first delivery.

**Article 5 — ending the agreement.** Only the client may end the programme, and the desk records the request for the client to confirm; notice is the number of calendar days printed against the tier.

**Article 6 — what falls due at closure.** Where the closure day falls before the end of the term, the early termination charge printed against the tier falls due; the equipment collection charge printed against the same tier falls due either way, and the deposit is returned net of anything outstanding.

## Points of judgement on these articles

Question: the client asks for deliveries to stop for a period shorter than the minimum printed against their tier.
Answer: a stoppage of that length is handled as a skipped delivery rather than as a pause.

Question: which charges at closure turn on where the closure day falls, and which do not?
Answer: the early termination charge printed against the tier is attached to a closure day falling before the end of the term; the equipment collection charge printed against the same tier is stated to fall due either way. The deposit is returned net of anything outstanding.

Question: the programme stands as a proposal and the client no longer wants it.
Answer: a proposal is withdrawn rather than paused.
